fact: ESCOM (Electricity Supply Corporation of Malawi), in its own 7 Oct 2025 slides, describes an operating ESCOM data centre in Blantyre offering cloud computing, physical hosting (rack space and bare-metal servers) and virtualization to customers, open to government and private clients; 2 modules of 21 racks, 595TB storage, 99.98% uptime. No opening date is given, so as_of is the document's publication date.

The National Data Centre in Blantyre, built by Huawei and run with the Ministry of Information and ESCOM, was launched in July 2022 and by February 2024 hosted 78 virtual machines, each for one client, with ESCOM reporting demand from both government bodies and the private sector.

Government ministries, departments and agencies use the National Data Centre, which Huawei built and which Huawei, the Ministry of Information and ESCOM oversee, to hold clients' data and services on 78 virtual machines, so critical information stays in the country rather than offshore; the article gives no date other than its publication date of 2024-02-10.

TNM states it acquired OpenConnect Limited's Tier 3 data centre at Kanengo, Lilongwe, for K12 billion, to be integrated with its Limbe data centre and offer Data Centre as a Service; the tier is stated by the company, with no certification named; as_of is the 2026-09-11 handover, the document's date.

Sparc Systems launched a new data centre in Lilongwe offering affordable hosting services to large enterprises and smaller firms, per its managing director; as_of is the article's published date as no launch date is given.

Sparc Systems unveiled its new Lilongwe data centre, with capacity for up to 120 racks, to provide secure data hosting for institutions inside and outside the country; as_of is the article's published date as no launch date is given.

The COMESA IDEA half-year report (Jan-Jun 2026) states the Government national datacenter in Lilongwe is complete and that the Bomalathu platform has migrated to the National Data Centre, with a stop-gap expansion adding 115 TB of storage; it describes it as a Government data hosting facility, not one renting to outside customers.
The report describes the National Data Centre in Lilongwe as the Government of Malawi's own national datacenter, implemented under the state's Digital Malawi Acceleration Project.

The report states the Bomalathu Digital Services Platform has migrated to the National Data Centre in Lilongwe, which has a disaster recovery site in Blantyre, and that Government data hosting capacity was expanded by 115 TB.

The June 2026 request for bids says the Department of e-Government built a national data centre in Lilongwe, now existing and in use, and seeks to expand it for demand from government and other institutions (no date given, so published date used).
The request for bids says the Government of Malawi, through the Department of e-Government, built the national data centre in Lilongwe (no date given, so published date used).

The request for bids says the Government of Malawi's Department of e-Government runs the National Data Centre in Lilongwe, which hosts systems of ministries, departments and agencies, and is being expanded for government institutions' demand over at least five years (published date used).

The ToR says the Government of Malawi, through the Ministry of Information and Digitalization and the Department of e-Government, established the National Data Centre in Lilongwe, which will have 13 empty racks available for co-location; the document is dated January 2025 and gives no other date.
